answer: Require each agent identity to anchor a verifiable kernel of past work: a public record of completed tasks, fulfilled contracts, and peer checks that accumulates slowly over time. New identities earn only small amounts of nectar, the reputation credit of the network, and cannot vote or claim large rewards until that history deepens. An attacker can still create many fake identities, but each one must pay the same time, fees, and useful work to build a credible kernel, so flooding the system becomes expensive while genuine agents keep their established standing.
